scenes.heading: Logical deduction
scenes.say: All of Kai's cousins live in Bendigo. Lena lives in Bendigo. Is Lena his cousin? Not necessarily! Logical deduction is about using only the facts, and every one of them.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A detective uses only the clues found at the scene
scenes.science: You use only the facts given to decide what must be true
scenes.breaks: A detective can search for more clues. In the test you can't, so never add your own facts.
scenes.say: Think like a detective. A good detective only accuses someone if the clues prove it. You do the same: use only the facts given. The difference is that a detective can go looking for more clues. You can't, so never add facts of your own.

scenes.heading: Must, could, cannot
points: Must be true: true every time
Could be true: true at least once
Test 'must' by trying to break it
scenes.say: Must be true means true every time. Could be true means true at least once. Cannot be true means never true. To test a must, try to imagine a case where it's false. If you can, it's not a must.

scenes.heading: All works one way

right.title: Flipped (trap)
points: So Rex is a cat? No!

scenes.say: An all statement works one way, like an arrow. All cats are animals. Tom is a cat, so Tom is an animal. That's correct. But Rex is an animal doesn't make Rex a cat. He could be a dog. Don't flip the arrow.

scenes.heading: Draw a line
scenes.question: Ari before Bo. Cy after Bo. Di before Ari. Who finished first?
scenes.say: Ari finished before Bo. Cy after Bo. Di before Ari. Build a line one clue at a time. Ari, Bo. Then Cy goes after Bo. Then Di goes before Ari. So Di finished first. Ari looked first until the last clue.

scenes.heading: Use a grid
scenes.question: Dog, cat, fish. Ana's pet doesn't live in water. Ben's has no fur. Cara hasn't the dog. Who has the cat?
lines: No fur: Ben has the fish
Ana and Cara: dog or cat
Cara not dog: Cara has the cat
scenes.say: Three friends, three pets. Ben's pet has no fur, so Ben has the fish. That leaves the dog and the cat for Ana and Cara. Cara doesn't have the dog, so Cara has the cat.

points: Only the facts, all the facts
Draw a line or a grid
scenes.say: Recap. Use only the facts, and all the facts. Must means always, could means sometimes. All statements work one way only. And draw a line or a grid to keep track. Now try the practice questions!
